title: Normalized internal Hom arrows commute with a further coefficient extension
statement: Fix a prime $\ell$, an algebraic closure $\Omega/\mathbf Q_\ell$, and any scheme $W$. Let $P,Q$ be permitted common-stage Hom pairs with literal outputs and comparisons as in [def-weil-common-stage-internal-hom-data]. Let $L$ contain both output composita, and let $a:Q_{1,L}\to P_{1,L}$ and $b:P_{2,L}\to Q_{2,L}$ be arrows at $L$. Define $v_L(a,b)=\theta_{P,L}\,R\mathcal Hom_L(a,b)\,\theta_{Q,L}^{-1}$, using the prescribed comparisons of that definition. For every finite coefficient inclusion $L\subseteq M$, the stage-system transport of $v_L(a,b)$ equals $v_M(a_M,b_M)$, where both input arrows are transported by their recorded stage associators. This is equality of arrows at $M$, before passing to any common-stage quotient.

source.place: The existing commonStageDerivedInternalHom_existsUnique proof plan: compatibility of the displayed conjugation with further transport and eventual equality. The new obligation is only its one-extension equation.

proof.text: Use scalarHomOrdinary_naturality and the Hom clause of scalarOperationsOrdinary_tower for each input compositum, L and M. Conjugate by scalarCompletion, restrict to constructible objects, and rationalize. The uniqueness specifications of the rational comparisons identify these localized components with the published comparisons. Substitute the stage-system transition and associator clauses and the coefficient-inclusion composition law. The inverse first and forward second input associators cancel through Hom functoriality, giving the stated single-extension equation.

For the proved representative-independence corollary, equality of input classes gives eventual equality in each slot. Enlarge to a field above both equality witnesses. Apply the single-extension equation and mkHom_tr to both output representatives, substitute the two transported input equalities, and obtain equality of output classes. This step uses the actual upstream StageSystem quotient, with no faithfulness assumption.
